utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I did want to bring up some procedural matters before we had the witness in. The next witness will be Colonel Michael Phillips. He is a Rule 70 witness. Pursuant to your decision of 14 May, Prosecution was granted leave to add him as a witness. And you ordered certain conditions regarding his testimony. A, was that his testimony be limited to topics that were listed in Annex A to that decision. B, that cross-examination was limited to the scope of direct, and issues of credibility. C, that the witness could decline to answer certain questions on grounds of confidentiality. D, that representatives of the Rule 70 provider would be allowed to sit in. And I will indicate that there are two Your Honour, one is Ms. Karen Johnson and Elisa Skibsrud, S-k-i-b-s-r-u-d. And I believe the arrangements that are Ms. Skibsrud will be sitting next to the witness, and Ms. Johnson will be sitting beside us over here on the Prosecution side. And E - and this a remainder for myself, the Defence, and everyone else - that if there are questions concerning the contents of Colonel Phillips' notebook that those questions should take place in private session. Likewise if there's questions concerning his notes of his interview. And that any pages of those notebooks, if they are to be tendered into evidence, they should be tendered under seal. The Rule 70 provider then would review the transcript of any private or closed session and any documents tendered under seal with an eye to releasing as much as possible. I understand this was the same procedure that was followed with the witness Shaun Byrnes. And if there are no questions about that, Your Honour, then I have three other matters concerning some of the documents I want to use with this witness, if I can raise that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to seek leave to add seven documents, these are KDOM reports. The 65 ter numbers are 05354 through 05360. There are a total of seven of them. And my application would basically echo what Ms. Kravetz presented to Your Honours in connection with some KDOM reports that she sought leave to add at transcript page 8153. These are contemporaneous reports that were prepared by US KDOM. They relate directly to the evidence of this witness. They were all written, I think, in February and March of 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are these reports different from those Ms. Kravetz used?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, they're not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They are the same ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: They're from the same source. They were published on the website --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I mean, are they the same reports, or are they different reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: They're different reports for different days but from the same source and published on the US Department of State website and similar in all other fashion. Also we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I was going to get Mr. Djurdjic's reaction to that proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Let's go one thing at a time since Mr. Hannis raised a number of issues. I object to the introduction of these documents through this witness. This witness has nothing to do with the US KDOM, he was a member of the KVM, that is to say the mission founded by the OSCE. It has nothing to do with any KDOM reports. And he did not forward any such reports to the State Department. If I understood properly, he was an international official not a State Department official. To conclude, I think I have two out of the seven reports which are exclusively State Department reports, not even KDOM reports. The 6th and the 7th report, that is. We particularly object to those, and it encompasses the period which is not covered at all by the topics you set out. Also expanding evidence in such a way deviates from your decision and the decision as it stood in the Milutinovic case. Not even in the summary under 65 ter, the statement summary, mentions some of the things that we received in the e-mail we received yesterday from the Prosecution. If such evidence was supposed to be led and introduced, they should have used Mr. Byrnes who remained a KDOM member until the end working for the State Department at the same time. This witness did not work for his government, and such documents cannot be tendered through him. This is what we object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. In reply, I should indicate to my learned friend that the two he has the strongest objection to are 05361 and 05362; I'm not offering those, Your Honours. Those were reports for the 31st of March, 1999, and the 5th of April, 1999. Upon review, I saw that those were not from KDOM, those were State Department. They were posted after Colonel Phillips had left Kosovo, so I'm not tendering those. As for the others, yes, they are KDOM reports but I think the witness's evidence will be that he did receive these when he was working in KVM, he had a chance to review them. And what I propose to do with those is I want to show him some of the entries in there about general happenings in terms of activity of the VJ and the MUP in February and March 1999 and ask if that's consistent with what he personally observed and/or what he was getting from his own sources of information in KVM.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The documents proposed by Mr. Hannis to be added to the list will be added to the Rule 65 ter list. Can I be clear, Mr. Hannis, is it five or seven?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is seven, Your Honour. There were originally nine on my list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The two mentioned by Mr. Djurdjic would have made it nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good. Well it's seven that are added to your list, not nine?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct. Thank you. I would also seek leave to add 65 ter number 05364. This is a document which contains excerpts from Colonel Phillips' notebooks covering the time-period from 9 December, 1998, through 12 February, 1999. It's been disclosed to the Defence. This was something that we only -- I don't know the date, but we only recently received approval from the provider to us. I don't know if Mr. Djurdjic has any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Mr. Hannis knows better than I do what happened with these documents in the Milutinovic case. But since we realise that Mr. Hannis wanted to use these excerpts, we are going to as well. The Defence in the Milutinovic case used certain excerpts from the notes by Mr. Phillips. That is during the period when he was in Kosovo before the 19th of February, I think. That is the period that he is supposed to testify about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are quite correct, Mr. Djurdjic. Not only may you use this document, but you can use any of the other seven if you think it's of relevance to your case. They become available in the case being on that list. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be added to the list as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And lastly before we have the witness in, regarding his prior transcript when application was made to have him as a 92 ter witness, that transcript -- the full transcript including some closed-session portions was given the number P1215. Even though it has not been admitted yet. At the time, though, when it was uploaded in e-court, I think we inadvertently omitted ten pages because of a break when discussions were taking place during his closed-session testimony. We seek leave to add those ten pages. And then once I've gone through the appropriate questions with him about whether he can verify whether that's correct, then I will be moving to add P1215 as an exhibit under 92 ter. But that one would need to be under seal because it contains the closed session portions of his testimony. And then I need to seek leave to add 05343.01 which is a public redacted version of that prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Taking the bit we can deal with right now, the P1215 may have added to it the omitted pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And that concludes my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Splendid. Are we ready for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. While the witness is being brought in, could I just be sure that you are aware of our admonition yesterday to Ms. Kravetz that we must finish this witness by tomorrow evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, she did bass that on to me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not by tomorrow evening but by tomorrow at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. I may go into the second session today, but not very long, I hope. I believe that will leave adequate time for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You leave plenty of time for Mr. Djurdjic, that's the message.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on my previous experience with Mr. Hannis, I do not believe the last part of what he said. In any case, was this disclosed to the Defence? Was that a mistake concerning the ten pages of transcript which did not make the record? Did we receive the whole set? Yes, I guess so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can attempt, if you like, to prove Mr. Hannis a liar over this one, Mr. Djurdjic, but it's in your interest not to, I suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Now, I see you have with you the two representatives which have been authorised by this Chamber's decision. Ms. Johnson is aware of the procedure. Could I just indicate for your assistance that if you feel the need for any advice or if your advisor feels the need to offer you any advice, that can be done privately as you are situated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Press the off button on the microphone before you have that discussion. And if there is then -- you would then, in accordance with that advice, if there was any objection or difficulty, raise it, and we will then look at what it is and its nature and what role, if any, your visors may then need to play in the resolution of whatever it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And with a bit of luck, we won't have a problem. Mr. Hannis has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would indicate that sitting next to the witness is Ms. Skibsrud and Ms. Johnson is sitting behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us your name, please?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: My name is Michael D. Phillips. Do you want me to wear these head sets?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we both speak English, Mr. Phillips, I would ask if you would help me try to remember that we should take a pause between my question and your answer and between your answer and my next question so that the interpretation can keep up with us.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your occupation or your profession is?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I retired from active-duty air force yesterday, so I am currently an unemployed civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Congratulations or condolences, as may fit. How long were you in the air force?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: About 28 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And what was your rank upon retirement?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I retired as a full colonel in the air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you had a -- well, did you previously testify at this Tribunal in connection with the events in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999 in the Milutinovic case?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I believe that was in March of 2007. Have you had a chance to review a transcript of your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that it's true and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And would you answer those same questions in the same way if those questions were put to you today?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would at this time like to tender the full transcript, P1615 under seal, and 05343.01 the redacted version as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: First of all, the transcript itself will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01215 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The redacted transcript will also be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I see I misspoke and said 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wondered where 1615 came from. And the redacted transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The redacted transcript will be Exhibit P01303, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, can you tell us how you came to be in Kosovo in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: In 1998, I was stationed at pacific command in Honolulu Hawaii, and I had received a phone call in September from the vice-chairman of the joint chiefs of staff, General Ralston, telling me that they had just finished a session with Ambassador William Walker who had just been assigned to be the head of mission in Kosovo. And in that meeting he was asked is there anything that he needed, and when that question came he said, yes, he needed this air force lieutenant-colonel, I didn't know where he was assigned, that was me. And then I received a phone call a week later from General Ralston asking if I would be willing to give up my post in Honolulu to serve a tour with Ambassador Walker in Pristina, Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before I proceed further, I understand, Your Honours, that for 92 ter witness the practice is for the Prosecution to read a brief summary of the witness's evidence. And if I may, I would do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. This being a 92 ter witness, that would be the procedure to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. This witness worked as Chief of Staff for William Walker, the head of OSCE's Kosovo Verification Mission or KVM from November 1998 until July 1999. He provides evidence on the role of this mission in Kosovo. During his tenure in Kosovo, Colonel Phillips attended and took notes of meetings in which KVM head William Walker met various high-level officials of the FRY as well as with representatives of the VJ and the MUP. He also speaks about the engagement of VJ and MUP units in joint operations in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999. The witness recounts instances when KVM raised complaints with Slobodan Milosevic, Nikola Sainovic, General Loncar, MUP General Lukic, and other officials regarding the conduct of VJ and MUP units during those operations. The witness also provides evidence on the Podujevo incident in December 1998, on the Racak incident in January 1999, and on ongoing violations of October Agreements by the VJ and MUP. Colonel Phillips describes how the Serb forces steadily increased their presence and the level of their combat activities from January 1999 until the KVM was evacuated in late March. The witness also details visits to refugee camps in Macedonia and Albania after the evacuation and about the information reported to him and KVM from many of those refugees about how and why they left Kosovo and crimes committed against them by VJ and MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, I'd like if you could describe briefly for the Judges the general purpose of the Kosovo Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Sir, our mandate --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The last portion of the summary read by Mr. Hannis has to do with the refugees after their departure from Kosovo. That part was not within the 65 ter submission we received. This is an expansion of sorts that Mr. Hannis has just introduced. I don't know why and how. I followed closely what he was saying, and it is unclear to me. We don't find it in your decision either, Your Honours, in the first several points Mr. Hannis enumerated prior to the witness being led into the courtroom did not mention that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is information that we got from Colonel Phillips when we spoke with him during his proofing yesterday. We sent a supplemental information sheet to the Defence last evening advising them of that additional information. We had discussions with the provider about whether they viewed this as something that was covered by the topics we were allowed to raise, and the consensus was that this related to the non-compliance of the MUP and the VJ with the Holbrooke-Milosevic Agreements and the consequences of that non-compliance. It also relates to the actions of the VJ and MUP and their general modus operandi. And although Mr. Phillips would have been standing outside of Kosovo when he was talking to refugees in Macedonia and Albania, it does relate to events witnessed in Kosovo during the period of July -- or, November 1998 through July 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But not events witnessed by Mr. Phillips.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, but as I said, Your Honour, we took our understanding from discussions with the provider about whether or not their view was that this was covered by what they gave us permission to lead evidence on was it did relate to non-compliance of the MUP and VJ with the agreement

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, the Chamber would take the view that what Mr. Djurdjic has advanced has substance on this occasion. The list of topics which were set out in the annex of this Chamber's decision does not, on its usual understanding, nor on the understanding of the three authors who sit here, extend to secondary evidence the witness may have gathered after he had left Kosovo, even though it may relate to events that he was told had occurred in Kosovo. So I am afraid you need to limit his evidence to the other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, I think when we took out that intervention I had just asked you about what was the purpose of the Kosovo Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it was our understanding with the agreement that we were there to ensure that there was cease-fire maintenance in place and adhered to by both sides and which I refer to the KLA and the Serb, and the VJ and the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And when did you first arrive in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I arrived on the 4th of November, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was William Walker already there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: No, sir, I arrived with him, we flew in from Warsaw to Pristina airport where we departed the airplane and had an immediate conference at the airport stating what our mission was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How did you begin to go about your work in terms of contacting the Serbian authorities and trying to implement the agreement?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: The first few weeks after we arrived were really sent -- or spent trying to build the OSCE operation before we had reached out to any of the officials that were in Pristina representing the FRY. So it wasn't until, I think, early December we had our first meeting, we were invited to the government building where we met at that time Nikola Sainovic, Mr. Loncar, I believe General Lukic, Mr. Slana, Mr. Skoric, and others who introduced themselves to us and they would be assisting us and helping our mission move forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We have heard evidence in this case about a Federal Commission for Cooperation with the OSCE, are you familiar with that body or that name?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the name, but we had no direct meeting with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the gentlemen you described just meeting, this meeting was in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how -- do you recall how they introduced themselves to you? Can you tell us individually how that went?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Mr. Sainovic introduced himself very friendly as a personal representative of Mr. Milosevic. He introduced himself first. Our assumption was he was in charge there. General Loncar introduced himself as retired general but also as a representative of Mr. Milosevic. And Mr. Lukic introduced himself as the chief of police, the MUP, and I'm not a hundred per cent certain, but I believe he introduced himself the same way when he was also a representative of the Government of Belgrade referring to Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And after this meeting, did you have regular meetings with this group of men, Mr. Sainovic, General Loncar, and General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We tried to have meetings on a weekly basis. It didn't always occur that way, but we both had agreed that it would be advantageous to both sides to try and meet regularly to work any issues that had come up that were prohibiting the mission from standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And during your time in Kosovo before being evacuated in March, did you and Mr. Walker have any meetings with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We had two meetings, I believe one was in November and one was in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What can you tell us about those meetings and how they related to your mission with the KVM?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: The one I can recall, the first meeting, was a late November time-frame. We were delivering a letter that Ambassador Walker hand carried and delivered to him, kind of outlining what our understanding of the mission for the OSCE was. And the second meeting that we had in December was a meeting, I believe Ambassador Miles attended with us. And that meeting regarded non-compliance issues that were prohibiting and hindering the OSCE Mission from standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned Ambassador Miles, can you tell us who he was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I referred to him as ambassador, but at the time he was a charge d'affair for the American Embassy in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned a letter that was delivered to Mr. Milosevic at that first meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: It was -- it was a letter of outreach. There was a lot of discussion prior to the November meeting with Mr. Milosevic on the interpretation of the agreement. Both sides were interpreting it in a different manner, and it was an attempt by Ambassador Walker to achieve a common understanding of the intent of what the mandate was. And it also had in there, I believe, some request of Mr. Milosevic requesting his assistance to get some things from a security aspect, from a -- we wanted to move the visa process along so from a consulate request aspect to try and set up the mission. So we had a few requests and a common understanding with what the purpose of the mission was, what we were going to try to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to put up an exhibit for you to look at. It's P838.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It should be appearing on your monitor shortly, sir. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: This is a letter that Ambassador Walker carried forward to Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. On the first page we see there some definitions of the terms that OSCE proposed to be used in interpreting the agreement?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is in evidence already, Colonel, but we see here there are a request for certain kinds of information from the FRY about the security forces and requests for certain kinds of notifications?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were all these discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the last page, just to complete the document. Well, that's the attachment. I was looking for the signature page. I thought it was the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what was Mr. Milosevic's reaction to receiving this letter some time shortly after the 23rd of November?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: As I recall - it's been a long time, it's been ten years - our first meeting, we arrived and he met us at the car and very friendly. The first meeting generally went well. A lot of discussion over definitions and, as I recall, we really never got an agreement one way or the other from Mr. Milosevic. So I believe we kind of walked away with, it was great to have the first meeting, glad that you are here, my representatives in Kosovo will work your needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who did you understand his representatives in Kosovo to be?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Loncar, and the group that I mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were any of them present at this first meeting with Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Mr. Sainovic, I believe, was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the second meeting with Milosevic, do you recall when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That was in December. I think December 15th roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, going back to the first meeting, where did that take place?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That took place at the White Palace in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The second meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: At the White Palace in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who was present for that one?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Sainovic also, Mr. Milosevic, Ambassador Walker, and, of course, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The purpose of the second meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That was a less friendly meeting. We had delivered information of non-compliance to Mr. Milosevic. And that was the purpose of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the nature of the information and non-compliance?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We weren't getting -- we weren't receiving our consulate that was promised to us - we were getting stood up - so we could get the verifiers in on time in a quickened manner. We had requested some medical helicopter support, and we had requested the body guards for Ambassador Walker, armed body guards for Ambassador Walker, and those were not received well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: After that meeting on the 15th of December, did you continue to have meetings with Sainovic, Loncar, and Lukic in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For how long did that continue?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Really right up until about the time of mid-January when Racak took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And after Racak, any more meetings with those guys?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: There was a meeting or two with General Loncar, but I can't recall immediately if we had another one with Mr. Sainovic. I know he was difficult to reach after that. But the meetings were less regular and were often called in a reactive mode; when something had happened we needed to speak to the government folks immediately, but we did not any longer have any regular scheduled event after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You've mentioned telling Mr. Milosevic about non-compliance, were you also telling Sainovic and Loncar and Lukic about non-compliance issues?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you give us a breakdown of some of the general areas of non-compliance in KVM's view?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Well, there was an agreement that we would be provided some base-line information which we could verify, and we needed strengths of the MUP and the VJ, weapons counts. We needed to have our cars brought across the border without delay. We needed the consulate stood up. Just the logistics of the mission in general. We had -- we had asked for some of the more provocative patrols to be reduced. We had asked for troops in Malisevo to be reduced so we could bring back some of the IDPs. Those sorts of issues were the bulk of our discussions with Mr. Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to ask you about something called the Blue Book, are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look now at Exhibit P1029.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: While that's coming up, can you tell us what that was, who put it out, what was contained in it, what was its purpose?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: The Blue Book was a KVM document that was produced by the head of mission for operations referred to as Major-General DZ. And it was an overview of operational events of that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you see those reports on a regular basis in your position as Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the cover page that's on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you about just two or three entries in this document, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First I'd like to look at page 2 in the English. I think it's page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you seen this one before?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I have seen that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, was -- under the agreement, was there some requirement for MUP and VJ to notify KVM before undertaking certain operations?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I don't know that was specifically in the agreement that that was to happen, but we had had that discussion with Mr. Sainovic, the government building, that it was advantageous to both of us to have prior knowledge of an operation so we had some verification of both ongoing MUP and VJ ops in a particular village, and we were generally told - and this is kind of a good example here - generally the time that we got didn't coincide with the actual time of such an operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In discussion with Mr. Sainovic about this type of issue, was there an agreement on his part that they would provide that information to you?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was this the only time that happened where MUP notified you apparently after an incident had taken place instead of before?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: No sir, this happened on several occasions, and each time we brought it to General Sainovic's attention he would turn to General Lukic and ask him, you know, why this wasn't happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what Lukic said in those situations?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: He didn't often speak English in there, so I didn't get the direct interpretation of it. But what I do remember was that he would look into why the coordination was not happening, but he always blamed it on it was a coordination problem with the KVM.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could look next at page 48 in the English, page 50 of the B/C/S. I see Mr. Djordjevic [sic] on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic -- Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not have this exhibit on my list. I've been looking for it and I can't seem to be able to find it. I have organised everything here, and I'm really trying to find it but it's impossible. Of course, if it's not going to be used any more, that's fine, but we can move on and then get back to this later. I can't see the 26th of December. I do have the document of the 29th of December. Maybe it's my error, but I doubt it. Well, let's move on, I have seen the document and I'm look it up, if you're done with it. If you are not going to use it any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have two more entries from this document I propose to show the witness, I think the problem is that on the initial notification the document was listed as P1028. We sent a follow-up e-mail to indicate that should be P1029. I think the problem before that the pages were not uploaded in chronological order and a change was made to get them into chronological order for easier use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are quoting there Rule 65 ter exhibit numbers, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Those are admitted exhibit numbers, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, it seems that there may have been notification, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm informed that 1028 was MFI and 1029 was admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't have either 1028 or 1029 on my list, that's my problem. I mean, I only have documents starting with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have been informed that 1028 marked for identification is the whole of the book, was marked for identification because much of it has not been translated. Exhibit 1029 are those parts that have been translated and they were tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's my understanding, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't received anything for 1029. And as for P1028, I see that I have it on the list as P407.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis has told us about that, Mr. Djurdjic, that in the notification to you there was an error quoting 1028 and a follow-up e-mail told you it should be 1029. Carry on, please, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And for the record, that e-mail went out at 6.06 p.m. last night advising about the number change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought it was old history, it's new history is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very new history.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, can you see the page on the monitor now that is -- the heading is titled "Probable New VJ Unit"?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It makes reference to a unit wearing black berets?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you see any such unit or soldiers during your time in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We did see the VJ on occasion with a few wearing black berets, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What did you learn or what did you know about this unit?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We were to understand that they were kind of considered like Special Forces, kind of an elite force, kind of an anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were you able to learn anything about their equipment or weapons vis-a-vis other VJ units?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Just from an observation point of view they seemed to look, you know, the weapons they had were clean and new and they looked sharper and uniforms looked new and pressed. They were a good-looking unit. Well equipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Connected with that, let me ask a general question about MUP units you saw in Kosovo. Did you see a difference between various MUP units?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I kind of referred to it as there was the common beat-patrol MUP that you would see walking the streets in Pristina with a side-arm. And then there were what I call combat MUP who you would see in the field commonly wearing helmets and camouflage blue uniforms, flak vest, rocket packs on their back, long-barrelled weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the last entry in this document I want to show you is English page 91, I believe it's also 91 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You see that entry about "large VJ convoy observed"?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Appears to be dated the 16th of March, 1999. What can you tell us about that? Under the October Agreements, were there any prohibitions on what equipment could be brought in to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We were looking for both troop size, strength, and weapons to be reduced to pre-October numbers. And what we had observed really after the middle of January was a general increase in both VJ strength and on occasion MUP strength. We did see more armoured vehicles; the convoys were larger than we had traditionally seen in the November/December time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that a regular trend that you saw after December and January?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Middle of January the trend was, in my view from what I observed, an increase in those numbers. The convoys were larger and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see on the comment it makes reference to RC 2. Can you tell us what that stood for?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That was one of the five regional centres that we had split Kosovo up. We had OSCE commanders, if you will, in each one of the five with a small contingent of OSCE verifiers in each of the regions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall who was in RC 2?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The last sentence in that comment is: "Movement of M-84 assets into Kosovo is in clear violation of the base-line agreement."

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Right. Those were additional weapons, armoured vehicles that were being brought in that were beyond the mandate. The idea was to reduce, not to increase, and this was an increase.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do know what the M-84s were?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I believe they were tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's all I have with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And next I would like to ask you about KDOM reports. The first I'd like to look at is 05354. Were you aware of KDOM reports in 1998 and 1999 when you were in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what did you -- briefly, what did you know about KDOM, and how did it relate to KVM?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: When we arrived we knew that the KDOM -- there was an EU KDOM and a Russian KDOM and a US KDOM and that they were an American-only contingent, were not an international force. And we had no command and control over them. We met with Mr. Shaun Byrnes who was leading the US KDOM, but we did not use their reports to write our reports, but we were familiar with the KDOM reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you share KVM information with them?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I believe we did, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to review these reports during your time there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: The KDOM -- on occasion we did. We didn't make a daily habit out of reviewing them, but Mr. Byrnes made us aware of them and from time to time looked at them but more just as an interest item rather than a reporting item.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Have you seen -- well, the one that's on the screen now is from February 12th. I have a question for you about the fourth paragraph that says -- I don't think you can see it on the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll have to scroll down. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "The extensive VJ troop and equipment movements we reported yesterday resulted in about 50 villagers fleeing from their homes near Lapusnik in what the VJ labelled as an exercise. The troops moved into the villages firing weapons mounted on tracked vehicles." Were you aware of this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Not this particular incident, but this is consistent with that time-frame about the VJ and MUP moving into villages and creating widespread fleeing of the villagers. So not uncommon for that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And based on your -- your information and your own observations, from the KDOM reports that you looked at, did you see any information that was in direct conflict with your personal observations?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: In general they were reflective of being accurate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender 5354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01304.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next one, please, would be 5355.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Two things on this one, Colonel, dated the 19th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could scroll to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The first paragraph under the date mentions Rambouillet, and the second sentence says: "A visible increase in the movement of FRY, VJ, and police units and their equipment has been noted in the past 24 hours." You were aware of the negotiations that were going on in Rambouillet in February 1999?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you recall what the situation was in Kosovo in terms of the VJ and MUP activity?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: It was a very tense period. A number of VJ and MUP units were deployed throughout Kosovo resulting in a number of IDPs, displaced persons. But it was -- I would categorised it as -- try to characterise it as a period of -- it was a desperate period. We were fearful of losing a peaceful solution for a political solution in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think in the last paragraph there's mention of dead-line approaching in Rambouillet. And then it said: "Walker is scheduled to meet with General Loncar today to remind him of the FRY's responsibility for the safety of OSCE personnel in Kosovo." Do you recall what that was about at that time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We were concerned about our safety from day one, but generally that was anticipating evacuation of the mission. And we had built a contingency plan to evacuate the mission through a number of avenues of departure, and we wanted Mr. Loncar to know that if we did, in fact, evacuate that we were going to be safe in doing so and that he was to get that word out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to tender 5355, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01305.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, a few days later, 5356. 05356, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please switch off his microphone when not using it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is the 22nd of February, Colonel, and the fourth paragraph down, the last sentence: "There are reports also that the FRY is calling up reserve military units and arming some civilians over the past few days." Were you aware of that activity in late February of 1999?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The last paragraph in this report makes reference to KDOM mission having departed Pristina. Do you recall when that happened?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I was aware of it, but I don't have any real precise memory of that particular departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And it says: "... KVM remains on alert stand by status ..."

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was that a particular --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That was an alert stand by to be prepared to evacuate. The whole mission had been given procedures on what to do to evacuate, how much they could carry out with them, and where they were to meet. That's what that was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like to tender 5356.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01306.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And next if we could see 5357, 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, this one is dated the 11th of March, 1999. The second paragraph mentions reports that Serb VJ forces have conducted extensive sweep operations to the west of the Kacanik to Djeneral Jankovic highway. And mentions that these operations had forced villagers from their homes. Do you know where the Kacanik and Djeneral Jankovic highway was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I do. Yes, sir. It was in a mountain pass area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were you aware of this situation?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to tender 5357.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01307.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The next one is 5358, 65 ter number. I need the third paragraph in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, this short paragraph says: "Serb force levels have been augmented and remain poised throughout Kosovo for what may be a wider offensive against the ethnic Albanians." Was that consistent with what you observed around the 12th of March?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, this time-period, late February, early March is consistent with that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would tender 5358.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01308.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next is 65 ter 05359.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, this one is dated the 17th of March. And the first paragraph mentions: "As the peace talks continue in Paris, the apparent Serb military build-up in and near Kosovo continues." Was that what you were seeing?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I have to tell you, I was -- let's see, let me just read this just for a moment. I was at the peace talks in Paris during this time-frame, but this was an issue that was delivered at Rambouillet, not by me but it was brought up by Ambassador Walker. We were receiving reports from the OSCE Mission that was left while we were away, but that's consistent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would tender 5359.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01309.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And lastly, KDOM reports, 65 ter 5360.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First paragraph mentions: "... reports from the field that the Serbs continue to move sizeable reinforcements in and around Kosovo. As of yesterday, there were some 18-, to 21.000 troops poised just outside the province." And the second paragraph, the last sentence says: "The number of FRY and Serbian troops now out of barracks and in Kosovo and the introduction of new battle tanks puts Belgrade grossly out of compliance with the obligation it undertook last October." Were you aware of that situation?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would tender 5360.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01310.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, I want to talk a little bit about joint VJ and MUP operations or actions. Did you have occasion to personally observe any of that activity during your time in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the course of doing that, can you tell us a little bit about what you observed in terms of the different role of various MUP units. You described the difference between what you term the beat cop, something like the city policemen or the traffic policemen?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the others that appeared to be more combat ready, if you will?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where did you see combat MUP in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Wherever there was a village that was under stress by VJ presence or MUP presence, they were obviously there. But generally saw the MUP in the village proper and generally saw the VJ on the outskirts of those villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what kind of actions were these MUP combat units participating in, if you can describe?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: They were managing everything from check-points in and out of the village. They were house to house searching, in their view, for terrorists. That was related to us and subsequent meetings of such operations. They were making arrests. In general.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And based on those observations, do you know under whose command or direction they were operating -- deploying and carrying out these operations?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: It was our assessment that it was General Lukic who was directing the MUP activity in the villages of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to take any photographs of some of this activity that you observed?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to bring up now 65 ter number 02586.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this photograph, who took it, when and where, what's going on?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I took that photo. It was December time-frame in Podujevo. The blue personnel dressed in the camouflage blue there are MUP and the green is the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think you said this was near Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I believe it was near Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go to the next photograph, I think it's the third page in this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... of this one. Who took it, where, when?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I took the photo. I'm trying to recall exactly where it was. I'm not a hundred per cent certain, sir, but I believe it was also December time-frame, on the way into Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about this one?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yeah, I took that photo. I believe it was in Podujevo on December 1998 time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you write anything on the back of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I did, tried to an occasion, it took awhile to get photographs back so there was always a gap between when I took it and when I could record where I was with those.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we see the next photograph, K057-7165. It's still in this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about this one?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I don't believe this was near Podujevo. I want to say this photograph -- it was taken by me. I believe it was up near a place called Junik but not a hundred per cent certain on the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could I see page 6 of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about this one, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I took this one. This was a vehicle that had become stuck in the mud. I believe that was up near Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Same time-frame?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. December 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, next, page 8 of the exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tell us about this one.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I took this photo. I don't recall exactly where it was but this is the MUP. I was doing a search of some sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The tank that we saw in the earlier pictures, was it nearby when this picture was taken?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I don't recall, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Same question.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Podujevo, December 1998. I took this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And two more. The next page and the following, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your photograph?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I took this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Same place, same time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I believe Podujevo, December, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do these photographs accurately represent the working relationship you observed between the MUP and the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Yes, sir, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I would tender 2586, Your Honours.

utterances.text: Is that ten photographs all together?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe there are nine photographs and the back side of two photographs with some handwriting on them. We can look at the handwriting with this witness, perhaps just to be completely safe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should now, and then we'll receive the lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's pages 2 and 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's my writing on that screen, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything about this writing? The description doesn't sound like the photograph we looked at.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yeah, this was a mistake that I had made. I remember -- I remember the event, but it's on the wrong photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How about that, whose writing?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That is my writing, sir.

utterances.text: And does that accurately depict the second photograph that we had looked at in this series?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Militia -- when I use the term "militia," it's in my notes as well, I'm referring to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, I would tender that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I be sure of that last comment, are you saying that you referred to MUP as militia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On occasion I did, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you refer to anything else as militia other than MUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Those photographs, nine plus the two backs will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01311.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, I wanted to ask you about what is referred to as the Podujevo incident. Do you know what I'm talking about there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us when that took place approximately?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Roughly December 25th, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what was the nature of that event?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: It was on a sizeable VJ deployment. We were aware that it was going to happen. We were given notice. It was at an airfield location. We were told that the VJ were deploying up there for a normal training event, it was in their cycle. It was our understanding that they hadn't trained up there in some time, but they now in fact were training up there in good sized numbers with weapons, heavy weapons, artillery such as tanks and artillery. Also in the same time-period there was a heavy KLA presence in the area there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in KVM's view, was this a violation of the October Agreements?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I don't know that we necessarily say it was a violation. We found it odd that it was definitely provocative in nature. There had been some fire fight sporadic between KLA positions and some of the Serbian position, the VJ positions. But it was odd to see the -- a large number of VJ and MUP in that area at that particular time for training.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall this incident being the subject of discussions in your meetings with Mr. Sainovic, General Loncar, and General Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come back to that in a minute. I want to ask you about something else that happened shortly after Podujevo. In early January, do you remember an incident involving certain VJ soldiers who had gotten captured by the KLA and then eventually KVM being involved in trying to obtain their release?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Right, there were eight or nine VJ that had strayed from a normal patrol and were captured by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how did KVM get involved in this and what transpired, how did it come out?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: There was a meeting with Mr. Sainovic and General Loncar about it. We were asked to assist in getting their release. KDOM also was involved in getting their release. If I recall along the same time there were also captured KLA by the VJ, and we were working very hard to get both sides released. I recall meetings that we'd have Mr. Sainovic and then we'd have subsequent meetings but he had had to talk to Belgrade first, then get with us. And with the help of KDOM, KVM won the release, but I remember that we did not want to have the release appear that there was an exchange of prisoners. So I believe the VJ were released first by eight, ten days, and then later on the KLA were released and nobody was harmed. It was considered a pretty big victory for KVM, that KDOM helped facilitate. And I remember Mr. Sainovic and Mr. Loncar being very very happy and very high that this event had taken place. There seemed to be a sense of optimism that, you know, in his view that KVM was worth its salt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you characterise that probably as the high point of the cooperation between KVM and the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I would. I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the low point during your time there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Was the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And before the evacuation, was there something else that took place that was a significant drop down from the prisoner exchange, if you will?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Right, January 15th with the Racak incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just for right now just tell me briefly what that was and where Racak was?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Racak was a village just outside Stimlje, and it was the massacre of approximately 45 Albanian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know what Serbian units participated in that event, if any?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: The VJ was on the a bluff just outside the limits of Racak with heavy weapons, artillery, and tanks. And the MUP were down in the village and managing check-points in and out of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know if you detailed that before, but in describing the joint VJ/MUP actions, who did what exactly?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I observed both the MUP and the VJ at check-points. The VJ on the 15th had fired into the village with heavy weapons and occupied homes. And the MUP had gone -- after the shelling of the village, had gone in essentially house to house and were rounding up the young men and they separated them from children and the women.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know it's not quite the time for the break, but the next and last document I want to go over with this witness is 65 ter 05364, which are the excerpts from his notebooks which we need to do in private session, so I'm wondering if we might break a couple of minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sounds a practical idea, Mr. Hannis. We will adjourn now, we need to have our tapes rewound, and we'll resume at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may be seated. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I now request if we could move into private session; I want to look at excerpts from his notebooks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And this is 65 ter number 05364.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Colonel, I don't know, do you have a hard copy of the excerpts of your notebook? I think it's a 51-page document.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have those.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the first one I want to ask you about is at page 6 of the English, and this is actually at page 9 in the B/C/S. I will tell you and the Court that this appears to be from a 9 December, 1998, meeting based on the first page of the excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And DZ is speaking and you'll see the next -- the, well, near the bottom of the page right above where Sainovic is listed as speaking, someone is saying, I think it's DZ: "Our interpretation is far wider than the FRY interpretation, the definition and compliance is determined by KVM and not the FRY government." Do you remember that discussion at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And let me ask you a general question about these notes: How did you go about taking notes of all these meetings you attended in Kosovo in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I would attend the meetings and try and be as verbatim as I could in taking the notes. At the end of the evening, sometimes I would go back and try and fill in the gaps of those. But the purpose of the notes was intended for an end-of-evening discussion and for our own personal uses to record some of the past conversations for the next meeting. And they certainly weren't intended to be in this venue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. These -- this document I'm working with is a typed document. Your original notes, I take it, were not typewritten?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: No, sir. I hand wrote all my notes and these were transcribed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you have occasion to compare what's in this typewritten document or the typewritten version of your notes with your original notes to be sure that these are accurate?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have any doubt having looked at these typewritten notes about whether or not they accurately reflect what you wrote at the time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I have no doubt. They are pretty accurate. But that's to say, if I might, sir, that's to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: -- that there is not discrepancies which I have found myself in here of meetings and people that were at those meetings and so forth sometimes was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. And Mr. Sainovic is quoted or is noted as saying: "The 23 November letter is outside the agreement." Earlier in your testimony we looked at Exhibit P838, the 23 November letter from William Walker, is that what Mr. Sainovic is talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what Sainovic said at this meeting about how or why the 23 November letter was outside the agreement?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Well, he had always maintained that the OSCE agreement was the mandate and there was nothing else to supplement that. And he felt that the 23 November was a supplement to that agreement that hadn't been approved by any body of authority. So he really dismissed it, he didn't see it as a letter of any kind of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. At the bottom of the English page we see Walker's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And then if we can go to the next page in English, we can stay on the same B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Since Walker was the last thing written on the last page, I assume these next two are comments from him?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And he says: " I will notify NATO, Brussels, Warsaw, and Vienna of your intent to not honour the agreement." Who is he speaking to there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Mr. Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What about the next entry, did he say that during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Which entry are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "This meeting was very tension-filled..."

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Oh, okay. The first one. "I will notify NATO, Brussels ..." That's Mr. Walker speaking. The second entry there, the second meeting there was our -- my comment, not necessarily a word and then Mr. Walker saying that we want a base-line, no-notice inspection, but Mr. Minister, you're saying no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And we are to verify tension and feeling, what did that mean in the context, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That meeting was what I would define as a very emotional meeting. There was a level of frustration that had built-up over time. None of the requests that we had been asking for were being answered. And, you know, Mr. Walker was a fairly emotional man, and I think that this is a result to levy a threat of NATO and a threat of Brussels and of course the OSCE member states. And he knew that that was a sensitive point with FRY government because they wanted to be seen as a cooperative body in this effort. And he knew that was a - for lack of a better term - it was a button he could push to hopefully get some attention on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, did he make such a call the next day?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: No. I would have end up probably having to make that call, and I never made that call.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me turn next to page 14 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Sir, if I might just go back, I will say that issue and that meeting did come out in Vienna at an OSCE, I forgot the formal name of the meeting, but it came out when we addressed the member states with an update on how the mission was progressing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when that meeting was, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I don't. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go next to page 14 of the English and page 15 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel Phillips, that is a meeting that's listed as being 18 [Realtime transcript read in error "15"] September 1998 Sainovic, Loncar, and Slana. Who was Slana, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: He was an assistant of Mr. Sainovic that was typically at our meetings at the government building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could go to the middle of the page, you have S and is that Sainovic?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Saying: "It is in our interest that you chart our deployments of MUP and VJ units, FT is not a problem to get the data." Do you know what FT means there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Trying to find FT. I might be looking at the wrong paragraph here. Where did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Under B, we have an entry for someone B and then it is a paragraph that's about six --

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Got it. Okay. Yeah, I can't recall what FT refers to, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Future time? Forward time?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did -- he said that, but did he provide, subsequently, information about the deployments of MUP and VJ?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We got -- we got sporadic information on deployments, but Mr. Walker never received the base-line strengths that we had asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And on that same page, if you could go to the third paragraph up from the bottom, it's a two sentence paragraph, I think you've got your finger on it there, Sainovic or S: "We don't want you to be surprised about big units going somewhere. Sainovic will provide copies of additional map with MUP and VJ locations." Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
