We also raised it with the KLA in meetings at a place called the Ice House that this was not helpful for -- our advantageous to them to be doing this. We had no major to turn off funds. All we could do was to carry that. We could levy the protest with the KLA and give that to the OSCE to help us with.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. During your stay in Kosova and Metohija, did you have any information or knowledge that the Republic of Albania was providing logistical support to the Kosovars in terms of providing training and assisting them in supplying weapons, running weapons, to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We had knowledge that this was occurring. We had knowledge that there was an Albanian in Switzerland that was funding the acquisition of weapons. I think they knew the individual's name. I can't recall off the top of my head, but we had knowledge that this was moving to Albanian. And we also knew that there were Albanians wanting to come back to Kosovo to join family and that the KLA was their ticket to get back into Kosovo, and the cost of doing so was to have them carry weapons across mountains and into Kosovo to provide to the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel, but my question related to the government and bodies, government bodies of the Republic of Albania that they actually facilitated this and provided logistical support on their territory to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I have no idea what the Government of Albania knew or didn't know. I just had knowledge that it was occurring, but I don't know what the government knew in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the Yugoslav authorities did not inform you of this?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yugoslav authorities did. It was a discussion that we had with Mr. Sainovic. It was a great concern of theirs, and so we were aware of their concerns. But as for the government, if you are asking me if the FRY had information from the Albanian government, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the KVM staff conclude that the KLA actually engaged in whatever their activities were on the territory of Albania without the knowledge and support of the Albanian government?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I think -- if you are asking me my opinion here, my opinion is is that I believe the Albanian government was aware of KLA activities. And naturally being the case, what their stated goals were, the Albanian government was fairly passive in what the KLA was doing. They neither stopped it or came out and publicly supported it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, my question to you is, because you were a witness, you actually attended the meetings of the highest leadership, the top leadership of the KVM in Pristina, and my question really relates to whether there was any position taken by the KVM on these complaints that were raised by the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: We agreed with the FRY; it had to stop. It was not helpful for us, for our mission, it was not helpful to the FRY. And it was hurting the KLA. And so we were in full agreement that this funding of weapons needed to stop. We suggested that both within the OSCE member states and when Ambassador Walker and I went back to Washington, that that was an issue that needed to be curtailed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you inform the president of the OSCE, the OSCE Secretariat, and perhaps the Security Council, the UN Security Council thereof?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: My memory says to me that we -- we did inform the OSCE member states in a briefing to all members. I can tell you that we did inform Secretary Albright. We did inform Mr. Walt Slocum who was Department of Defence for policy. And we did inform members of congress. As for the United Nations, I don't recall -- I would be surprised if we didn't on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of any practical steps taken to cut these channels through which the weapons were funnelled into Kosovo and Metohija from Albania while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: From a KVM perspective or from a policy perspective of the United States? I'm unaware of -- how best to word this. It was clearly something we didn't want to happen. We sought help from the OSCE member states, but I'm -- I'm unaware of any actual steps that were taken to prohibit that. It was very hard, being a small mission, we never grew to 2.000 people to get us out on the border. And so I'm unaware -- in the case of KVM the practical steps would have been, you know, we go to the primary LOCs and have our own check-points and prohibit those weapons from coming in. The best we could do was to speak to the KLA commanders that this needed to stop. It was provocative and not helping. So we did give some verbal warnings. We did that at the Ice House to people like Sokol Bashota, Krasniqi, other KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the next page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, would you please look at 4(a). Paragraph 4(a). Would you agree with me that this paragraph calls on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to cease all action only in relation to the civilian population and to withdraw its security units that are used for civilian repression?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: I would agree with that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now look at 5 -- item 5, sub-item (b). Am I correct that the Republic of Yugoslavia is called not to carry out any repressive actions against the peaceful population?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: That's what the document says, so, yes, I agree with that. Peaceful population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that this Security Council document was the document underpinning the next document, the verification mission document of the OSCE, I'm not sure whether we have time to see the other document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just pull it up on the screen, P835, to jog the witness's memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Colonel, based on the format, perhaps you can't recall this document, but do you recall its content?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Colonel, this is a document dated 16 October 1998 signed by the minister of foreign affairs of the FRY, Zivadin Jovanovic, and Mr. Bronislaw Geremek who at the time was the presiding of the OSCE, and this was the document that facilitated the verification mission, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MICHAEL PHILLIPS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is the time when we should end for the day because I have a few more questions remaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have run your time indeed, Mr. Djurdjic. We must adjourn, and we continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. We must ask you to return tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Court Officer will assist you and those advising you when we rise. Now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
